verdict.rationale: Sprinto documents its own API Playground, a browser-based GraphQL explorer for exploring the API schema and testing queries and mutations in real time. Introspection also lets the schema describe itself. However, the playground needs an administrator account and a valid API key, runs against the live tenant, and no pre-built runnable examples or sandbox are documented. The explorer returns 403 to non-browser clients, so runnability rests on vendor docs only. Missing for 10: documented runnable example snippets in the reference, ungated or sandboxed access separate from the live tenant, a downloadable spec (OpenAPI paths 404), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The Sprinto API Playground is a browser-based GraphQL explorer that lets you interact with the Sprinto Developer API without installing any client libraries or GraphQL tools
You can use the playground to explore the API schema, test queries and mutations, and validate responses in real time.
Introspection allows the API to describe its schema, including available queries, mutations, and response types.
